name: Graphite

paragraphs: A Graphite miner sends routes for one or more vehicles to validators, who are participants that score the miners' work, or proposes swaps to rebalance a portfolio. The listed minimum is four 2.5 GHz x86-64 cores, 8 GB of RAM, 4 GB of swap and 10 GB of free disk, with 100 Mbps in each direction. A CPU is sufficient, and the miner needs a reachable port and a registered Bittensor hotkey, which is the key a miner works with. The separate Taotrader guide requires an account and a balance of 5 to 15 TAO.

Validators compare valid routes with a benchmark and other replies, while portfolio scores give 60% weight to using fewer swaps and 40% to meeting allocation targets. When the published validator submits weights, it overrides those scores and gives UID 20 all its weight. The Taotrader guide describes hourly scoring, 300 blocks for adjustments and a 6,900-block trading restriction.

The guide describes a 60/20/20 split, but the code starts only the synthetic request loop, and synthetic batches start more than 25 blocks apart. Route replies get 30 seconds plus graph reconstruction time, while portfolio deadlines scale with the numbers of portfolios and constraints. The guides give no registration protection period or additional graph-mining fee. Read from https://github.com/GraphiteAI/Graphite-Subnet at commit 503b551 on 2026-11-23.
mining_note.how_it_was_made: This note was put together by AI agents and not by a person who mines here. One agent read the subnet's public repository and wrote down what a miner does, what it takes and how the work is paid, with a source for each statement, and a second agent opened every source and took out whatever it did not support. Of 23 source checks, 23 held, 0 did not hold and 0 could not be opened, and only what held is in the text above. Nothing of the subnet's code was run, and the note describes the code as it stood on the day and at the commit named in its last sentence, so it can be out of date.
